claim: In a head-to-head non-developer test, Lovable and v0 produced a working photo-booth app from a single prompt while Bolt failed across six attempts with the camera feature never loading.
quote: Both Lovable and v0 delivered fully working photo booth apps from a single prompt. Bolt failed to produce a functional app despite six attempts, with the camera feature never loading properly.

claim: Designlab's 2026 non-developer guide ranks Lovable as the most hand-held, visual, polished chat-first option with one-click deploy, hosting, and auth handled automatically.
quote: the answer when 'answer' means the most visual, polished, hand-held option ... You describe what you want in chat, Lovable builds a polished, full-stack app

claim: Bolt.new is described as the speed demon of the category, taking users from blank page to live app in under a minute, but its outputs look great as demos rather than long-term apps.
quote: the speed demon of the category ... go from blank page to live app in under a minute ... Bolt apps look great as demos but aren't really built for long-term maintenance

claim: Altar.io's 2026 founder comparison says Lovable hides almost everything technical and is the workshop pick because non-technical founders exposed to Replit's file tree get overwhelmed and migrate to Lovable.
quote: non-technical founders get overwhelmed and migrate to Lovable

claim: Lovable's own comparison concedes Bolt has the lowest barrier to entry for a complete novice because it needs no accounts or configuration, while Lovable introduces backend concepts (tables, auth, RLS) early.
quote: For someone who has never written code, Bolt has the lowest barrier to entry ... Open a browser tab, type a prompt, see a result. No accounts to connect, no configuration screens.

claim: Bolt.new generates simple landing pages in 2-4 minutes and basic to-do apps in 8-12 minutes, with built-in one-click deploy to a .bolt.host URL with SSL or one-click publish to Netlify.
quote: Simple applications like landing pages typically generate in 2-4 minutes, while basic to-do apps take around 8-12 minutes ... Bolt offers built-in hosting that publishes your project to a .bolt.host URL instantly with SSL included.

claim: Cursor is judged unsuitable as a first tool for complete beginners in 2026 because it presents a full IDE with file tree and assumes some grasp of project structure; reviewers recommend Lovable first.
quote: If you've never opened a code file before, it's recommended to start with Lovable or another beginner-friendly tool first. Cursor has a steeper ramp but rewards that investment.

claim: The imagi x Lovable Hour of AI program ships a 60-minute, no-account, no-setup classroom curriculum where grade 6-12 students vibe-code a catching game on Lovable, the only major vibe-coding tool with a real K-12 classroom track in 2026.
quote: In this 60-minute Hour of AI lesson, learners use Vibe Coding on Lovable, guided by imagi's ready-to-teach curriculum — no accounts, no setup hassle

claim: Claude Artifacts (and its 2026 generative UI mode) actually render and run apps inline, while ChatGPT Canvas only shows code without executing it, making Artifacts the stronger of the two for instant-gratification workshop demos.
quote: Claude's generative UI is an execution environment designed for building and running ... If ChatGPT writes a JavaScript application in Canvas, you're looking at the code — not using the app.

claim: Claude Artifacts 2.0 turns prompts into working in-chat apps in minutes with no coding, but reviewers say it only gets a beginner about 70% of the way to a real shippable app, with no native one-click deploy to a public URL.
quote: Claude Artifacts gets you about 70% of the way to a working app – the last 30% usually requires professional development for production quality

claim: v0 is a UI-only generator that assumes Vercel familiarity and is not a full-stack builder; it's described as the wrong starting point for someone without a Vercel account or developer knowledge.
quote: If you don't already have a Vercel account or developer knowledge, v0 is the wrong starting point

claim: Lovable has positioned itself as the default platform for non-coder hackathons in 2026, with the BDAA x Lovable Hackathon explicitly branded "a hackathon for builders, not coders."
quote: BDAA x Lovable Hackathon: A hackathon for builders, not coders.
